subject: Proposal: 2027 renewal — commit realignment + on-ramp incentive
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Samir Rao <samir@pelotonix.com>
Cc: Emily Torres <emily.torres@pelotonix.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: 2027 renewal — commit realignment + on-ramp incentive

Hi Samir / Emily,

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. Based on Pelotonix’s Q3 usage and the goals you shared for expanding ML features in 2027, I put together a renewal proposal that balances unit economics for you with predictable capacity for Redwood. High level:

- Term & commit: 12-month term with a revised commit of 1.2M token-units (up from current 900k), with true-up at year-end.
- Price hold: 12-month price hold on unit rates for the committed volume.
- On-ramp incentive: 3-month usage credit equal to 20% of invoiced usage (applies to overage and initial burst).
- Credits & flexibility: $75k one-time credit to be applied at signing in exchange for a three-quarter payment schedule; ability to burst above commit at a predictable overage rate capped per month.

I attached the redwood-renewal-offer-v3.pdf and a usage-runbook.xlsx that shows historical token patterns and an estimated projection for your new features.

Ask: can you review the attached and confirm whether you can get internal alignment on the 12-month price hold + 1.2M commit? If that’s too aggressive, we can discuss a shorter hold or a two-year smaller-commit path. Happy to jump on a call — propose Wed 22nd 10am PT.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Director, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-renewal-offer-v3.pdf, usage-runbook.xlsx

From: Samir Rao <samir@pelotonix.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Pelotonix Procurement <procurement@pelotonix.com>, Emily Torres <emily.torres@pelotonix.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: 2027 renewal — commit realignment + on-ramp incentive

Laura — thanks for the clear proposal. A couple quick items from our side before we escalate: 

1) Price hold length: our finance team is okay with a price hold, but 12 months is the ask from your side — we'd prefer 6–9 months unless we can get a lower committed unit rate. Any flexibility on shortening the hold in exchange for a higher upfront commit?

2) Compliance evidence: procurement needs the SOC 2 report and a short note on data residency for our VPC usage. Can you surface those?

3) On-ramp credit: the 20% credit is generous; we need to confirm how it applies to overages vs committed usage — can you clarify mechanics (credit cap, minimums)?

Looping in procurement to keep things moving.

—Samir
Head of Platform, Pelotonix
samir@pelotonix.com

Subject: Re: Proposal: 2027 renewal — commit realignment + on-ramp incentive

Samir — great questions. Answers below and a suggested compromise.

1) Price hold trade-off: if Pelotonix can commit to a larger upfront guarantee (1.35M token-units paid 50% at signing, 50% at 90 days), Redwood will agree to a 9-month price hold. Alternatively, we can keep the 1.2M commit and hold for 12 months — but that would require the $75k up-front credit reduction to $50k.

2) Compliance: SOC 2 Type II and our VPC configuration notes are here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cPelotonixRenewal (I've shared the SOC2 PDF and an architecture note). If procurement needs the attestation letter, Rafael (cc'd) can provide the most recent report.

3) On-ramp credit mechanics: 20% credit applies to billed overage and burst consumption outside the committed monthly cadence, capped at $60k for the 3-month on-ramp window. Credits apply as invoice line-item adjustments.

If that compromise sounds reasonable, I can have a redline-ready DocuSign agreement sent to procurement. Proposed calendar for a short alignment call: Wed, Sep 22 at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Attachments: redwood-renewal-offer-v3.pdf (updated)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: 2027 renewal — commit realignment + on-ramp incentive

Team — forwarding the Pelotonix replies and my proposed compromise (see below). Quick negotiation play:

- If they go for the 1.35M upfront (50/50), we give the 9-month price hold + keep $75k credit. If they push back on upfront cash, accept 1.2M + 12-month hold but reduce credit to $50k.
- Offer a +5% discount on committed unit rate if Pelotonix agrees to participate in a brief case study and a joint blog post in Q1 2027 (marketing value).
- Reserve the right to limit burst to 200% of committed monthly average during the on-ramp period to protect capacity SLOs.

Monica — can you put together a short slide showing the projected token burn under the 1.35M commit vs current run-rate (use usage-runbook.xlsx) so procurement sees the math? Alex — can you lead pricing if they request a blended rate? Rafael — please confirm we can provide the SOC2 attestation link and any redaction rules.

I'll hold on sending the DocuSign until we have the final signal.

Thanks — Laura

Attachments: recommended-redlines.docx, usage-runbook.xlsx

Subject: Re: Proposal: 2027 renewal — commit realignment + on-ramp incentive

Laura — thanks for working through options. We had a final sync with finance and procurement this morning and can accept the 1.35M commit with 50% up-front and the 9-month price hold, subject to standard procurement redlines. We also agree to the case study ask (we'll coordinate with marketing).

Next steps: please send the DocuSign with the agreed economics and the redlines you propose. Procurement will route the DocuSign and return with any legal redlines. Also can we schedule the kickoff for Oct 6th — 30 minutes to align on rollout?

I've attached Pelotonix's redlines for your reference (pelotonix-redlines.docx).

—Samir
